statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-39882 (GO-2026-4985, GHSA-w8rr-5gcm-pp58): the OpenTelemetry-Go OTLP HTTP exporters did not limit the size of the HTTP response body read from the collector, so a malicious or misconfigured collector could exhaust memory. go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp is fixed in v1.43.0: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-w8rr-5gcm-pp58, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4985, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/8108, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/v1.43.0. Read every published alertmanager-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 to the current 0.35.0-r2, each for x86_64 and aarch64. Each package installs two files, /usr/bin/alertmanager and /usr/bin/amtool, statically linked Go programs with no program interpreter, built with CGO_ENABLED=0. The versions below are read from their Go build information and are the same for both programs and both architectures in each build. They list otlptracehttp v1.39.0 in 0.31.1-r0 to 0.31.1-r5; v1.43.0 in 0.31.1-r6 to 0.33.1-r5; v1.44.0 in 0.34.0-r0 to 0.34.0-r5; v1.45.0 in 0.34.0-r6 to 0.35.0-r2. /usr/bin/alertmanager links the trace exporter (otlptracehttp.New and the client's UploadTraces) in every build. Neither program's Go build information lists the metric or log HTTP exporters (otlpmetrichttp, otlploghttp) that the advisory also covers. Builds 0.31.1-r0 to 0.31.1-r5 carry a vulnerable otlptracehttp; 0.31.1-r6 and every later build carry v1.43.0 or later. The range ends at 0.31.1-r6.
